newsitem.title: USA: Lott would prefer no US cigarette tax rise in bill.
newsitem.headline: Lott would prefer no US cigarette tax rise in bill.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said that he would rather there was no cigarette tax increase in tax legislation passed by the Senate earlier on Friday.

The Senate bill would raise the cigarette tax by 20 cents per pack. The House tax bill does not include that provision and the issue will be dealt with when House and Senate negotiators meet to work out differences in the two bills.
"I would prefer not to have it," Lott, a Mississippi Republican, told reporters. "But it will obviously be something we will have to consider," he said.
Lott said he will be among the negotiators working on a compromise tax bill and that he would not feel obliged to support a cigarette tax increase at that time.

Lott said he had felt obliged to back the tobacco tax increase in the Senate Finance Committee and on the floor of the Senate, but in the coming negotiations, "I don't feel like I have to support it."
